ev.q: Using 2021 Medicare Part D data, CDC examined prescription volumes, rates, and costs for topical antifungals
the highest prescription rate was in the Northeast (188.0 prescriptions per 1,000 beneficiaries), followed by the South (138.1 per 1,000)
Among all topical antifungal prescriptions, 44.2% (2.9 million) were written by the top 10% (13,106) of topical antifungal prescribers.
The highest average per prescription costs were for efinaconazole ($1,035.38), tavaborole ($784.63), and oxiconazole ($729.84)
During 2021, approximately 6.5 million topical antifungal prescriptions were filled (134 prescriptions per 1,000 beneficiaries), at a total cost of $231 million.
The number of prescriptions per provider was highest for dermatologists (87.1), followed by podiatrists (67.2), and primary care physicians (12.3).
Total prescription volumes were compared between higher-volume prescribers (top 10% of topical antifungal prescribers by volume) and lower-volume prescribers.

equity.level_reason: No social-position dimension is analyzed; comparisons are by drug, provider type, prescriber volume and Census region (geography, not an SPD). Age ≥65 appears only in the program's general eligibility description.
equity.equity_measurement: Census region differences are geographic only; 'more ready access to medical care' is offered for the Northeast but is not tied to social position.

notes: Design inferred (none named): descriptive analysis of aggregated claims data. Higher-volume share is reported within each provider type, read as comparison rather than stratified. Enrollment dataset supplies denominators only.
view_issues: Methods sentence is garbled ('calculated by drug and region and to calculate prescription rates per 1,000 beneficiaries by drug and region'). 'Top 10th percentile' is used for the top 10% of prescribers.
